source.title: Distance Is Not Enough: Forget-Retain Alignment Gap Predicts LLM Relearning Robustness
source.authors: Yi Chen; Hanna Hsieh; Shu-Hong Liu; Chuan-Bo Hua; Zi-Han Ma; Kun Wang; Joo-Young Kim

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether fine-tuning attacks restore forgotten behavior after unlearning, using post-attack extraction strength and accuracy across methods and settings; it also evaluates FRP as a counter-method.
record.gate_note: Rows report the study's own post-unlearning fine-tuning attack results. Cited results from prior work are not included. Values in the main TOFU table are averages over three forget-set sizes within each model. The paper also reports utility, but the rows below focus on the main recovery measures; it does not state an accuracy chance level for TOFU.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own fine-tuning relearning attacks (retain, forget and forget+retain sets; one epoch, lr 1e-5, AdamW) on GA, GradDiff, NPO, RMU, SP and its own FRP. It measures post-attack extraction strength on TOFU and MUSE-News, and 4-way accuracy on WMDP-cyber. These results bear directly on B, on the no-recovery part of A, and on F through FRP. None of the original sources is this paper.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that relearning robustness depends on which weights move, not global displacement. FRAG predicts robustness better than L2, and FRP improves resistance to relearning at an explicit utility cost, tracing a robustness-utility frontier. They also state that given enough epochs every method eventually gives the knowledge back.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates fine-tuning relearning attacks and introduces FRP, a pruning-based unlearning method; it does not reproduce a single original unlearning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack data source matters: the authors report forget+retain as the strongest attack, with retain-only and forget-only often weaker. Learning rate and optimizer affect attack effectiveness; the authors report that some settings do not recover knowledge or collapse utility. Longer horizons increase recovery. FRP's pruning sparsity and retain penalty trade forgetting against utility.

fits_no_version.finding: FRAG, a training-free weight-alignment score, correlates with ΔES under forget+retain attack (pooled Spearman -0.78, versus -0.36 for global L2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robustness of unlearning to relearning can be predicted from whether the update targets forget-critical and spares retain-critical weights.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are given for the reported table values. Experiments cover TOFU, WMDP-cyber, and MUSE-News and several model families, but the authors note that broader benchmarks, multilingual data, and larger architectures remain future work. FRP incurs a larger MMLU drop than RMU and SP in the reported Qwen comparison. Some attack variants are explicitly ineffective or harm utility.
record.rows_left_out: The main TOFU table's separate ΔES and utility columns are not recorded as additional rows. Other appendix sweeps and attack variants (Tables 10–12 and 14–20), including learning-rate, optimizer, attack-data mixture, matched-control, and predictor analyses, are omitted to keep the row set focused on the principal recovery outcomes; the longer-horizon outcomes from Table 13 are retained. Table 8's Qwen entries duplicate the WMDP-cyber results in Table 2.

untested.parts: No method is shown first reaching near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy. TOFU uses ES, which has no chance level. On WMDP-cyber, only the degenerate GA/GradDiff/NPO runs and Zephyr RMU (0.270) reach about chance.
No activation-direction ablation or access-blocking analysis is run.
No prompting-only, jailbreak, cross-language or in-context attack is run.
FRP is tested only against fine-tuning relearning. It is not tested against activation edits, quantization or prompting attacks.

missing.what: Paraphrase, 50/50 mix and forget+general attack-data results. Paraphrased forget data barely recovers RMU, NPO or FRP, which bears on B's loosely related relearning sets.
Optimizer and learning-rate sweeps. SGD and SGD with momentum recover nothing, Adafactor collapses utility, Adagrad recovers RMU to 0.597, and 5e-6 lr recovers little.
MUSE-News retain-only attack ΔES on LLaMA-2-7B: GradDiff +0.313 (collapsed), RMU +0.205, SP +0.072, FRP +0.067.
Per-split TOFU results, e.g. RMU 3B forget05 retain attack only +0.019 while forget+retain gives +0.678. Shows that retain-only attacks can understate recovery.
Matched-utility comparison: FRP recovers 1.9-4.9x less than RMU at equal utility.

record.verdict_notes: The A and B labels exclude GA because its averaged rows include collapsed checkpoints, and exclude the Zephyr degenerate baselines. TOFU ES has no chance reference, so A's near-chance premise is untested there. Row states are relative to B (recovery); for F, low recovery is the supporting outcome. Table 13 uses different RMU/NPO checkpoints from Table 9.

versions.untested_parts: TOFU uses extraction strength, not targeted-knowledge accuracy, and the text gives no chance reference for that measure. The results do not establish that any method first reaches near-chance accuracy while preserving general ability.
The study tests fine-tuning on retain data, forgotten data, their union, and several other mixtures; it does not test rephrasing-only, activation edits, quantization, or prompting-only attacks.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis establishing access-blocking rather than deletion is tested.
No low-bit quantization attack is tested.
No prompting-only, rephrasing-only, jailbreak, language, or in-context-information attack is tested.
FRP is tested against fine-tuning attacks; it is not tested against activation edits, quantization, or prompting-only attacks.

relation.reason: Reports its own post-attack results on existing unlearning methods.

tranche.reason: Runs its own fine-tuning relearning attacks on several existing methods plus its new FRP method. The method differs from the original probe/GCG tests; the question is the same.

source_check.notes: Table 1's 'FRP (β=0.00)' rows equal the split averages of Table 9's 'FRP(β=0.05)' rows, and Table 6 gives β=0.00 ES 0.086 on 1B forget10, so the paper's β labels conflict. Gold drifts -0.001 to +0.022 in Table 1 but reaches 0.365 after 10 epochs (Table 13). Tables 10-13 use RMU/NPO checkpoints that differ from Table 9's.

statements.correction: 1B GradDiff ES: unlearned 0.123; retain 0.256, forget 0.264, forget+retain 0.441. Table 12 (forget10, 1B): RMU forget+retain 0.461, paraphrase 0.037, forget+general 0.047; NPO 0.137, 0.084, 0.099.
statements.problem: Gives no claim about this study. Its cited GradDiff rows don't show related text beating general text: forget-only roughly equals retain-only, and only forget+retain recovers clearly. Paraphrase also recovers little (Table 12).

statements.correction: LLaMA-3.2-1B RMU, TOFU avg over forget01/05/10, one epoch, lr 1e-5, AdamW, forget+retain attack: ES 0.105 -> 0.742 (gold 0.071). 3B RMU reaches 0.755.
statements.problem: The cited row fits 'large relearning sets' (forget+retain union is the study's largest attack set). But the conditions and why leave this study out, so readers can't tell it is a 1B TOFU one-epoch run.

statements.correction: WMDP-cyber retain-only attack: Qwen2.5-14B SP 0.515 -> 0.513; Zephyr SP 0.414 -> 0.407 (chance 0.25; Ref 0.583 and 0.446). On TOFU 1B SP ES 0.124 -> 0.171 (retain) and 0.237 (forget+retain).
statements.problem: SP is not left near chance. Its WMDP-cyber accuracy was never near chance before the attack, so no recovery means little. On TOFU, SP does recover.

statements.correction: Table 11 (forget+retain, 1 epoch, lr 1e-4): SGD leaves every method, gold included, at its pre-attack ES. Adagrad: RMU 0.035 -> 0.597, NPO 0.085 -> 0.208, FRP 0.062 -> 0.137. AdamW at this lr: RMU 0.134. Adafactor collapses utility.
statements.problem: The SGD and optimizer-dependence reading matches Table 11. The cited row T2-2 (SP, Qwen WMDP-cyber, AdamW retain attack) has nothing to do with optimizer choice. SGD was tried only at lr 1e-4 on TOFU forget10 1B, and the authors say it is not an effective attack.

statements.correction: TOFU ΔES for FRP 0.015-0.102 (1B/3B); RMU forget+retain ΔES 0.637 (1B), 0.700 (3B). WMDP-cyber: Qwen2.5-14B FRP 0.429 -> 0.417; Zephyr FRP 0.344 -> 0.376 (+0.032); Zephyr RMU 0.270 -> 0.424 (+0.154). Lr 1e-5, AdamW, one epoch.
